newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK PARLIAMENT PASSES CHANGES TO SECURITIES LAW.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK PARLIAMENT PASSES CHANGES TO SECURITIES LAW.

text.p: Slovak parliament on Wednesday approved a measure effectively reinstating securities trading outside organised markets, but rejected a controversial proposal which would have increased the power of majority shareholders.
Parliament agreed to reverse last year's decision which stipulated that all transactions must be registered on the Central Securities Registry and performed through brokers on organised markets.
Analysts said the new law effectively allows over-the-counter trading without registration on the main markets.
The Securities Act, originally amended last year, sets out ground rules for issuing and trading shares and bonds on the Slovak capital markets.
However brokers said last year's laws needed a thorough overhaul as, among other things, they did little to protect small shareholders and were incompatible with other related legislation.
The legislators however rejected one amendment which would have allowed majority shareholders to suspend trading of their shares on the stock exchange.

"But the amendments in fact bypass the issue (of shareholders' rights) and will considerably damage the transparency of the market," said economist Viliam Vaskovic, a deputy of the opposition Democratic Union.
